chunks: And from him, from Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman whose husband died, regarding her waiting period (iddah): if she stays in one house for a month or less or more, then moves to another, and stays in the new house for the same duration she stayed in the previous one, is this her practice until her waiting period is completed? He said: 'That is permissible for her, and there is no objection.'

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: A woman whose husband has died (widow)
key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection / it is valid

ai.seo_question: Can a widow change houses during her waiting period (iddah) and still fulfill the requirement?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies the flexibility of the widow's *iddah* residence, permitting her to divide her three-month waiting period across multiple homes rather than remaining in a single dwelling. This ruling underscores the practical ease (*rukhsah*) granted to widows during their mourning period, allowing them to adapt their living arrangements as needed while maintaining the integrity of the prescribed duration.
